newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, look for support.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, look for support.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased back 0.51 percent on Monday as investors continued to keep a low profile amid a dearth of trading incentives, traders said.

"Everybody is waiting for fresh foreign capital which is expected to come in May and push prices up. Until then shares will oscillate. This week the index may go up or down by a maximum of five percent," a trader said.
In February, the Bank of Slovenia blocked foreign trading by saying international investors had to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in securities.
The banks said they expect to open the first custodian accounts at the end of April or in May.
"In spite of poor volumes it seems prices have already bottomed out, therefore now may be a good time to buy shares," said one analyst, adding he recommends drug maker Lek and food company Droga.
"On the OTC market, drug maker Krka, trading firm Mercator and chemical producer Pinus would not be a miss. All these companies have good business results that should support share growth," he added.
The blue-chip SBI index fell 6.92 points to 1,343.86.
Issue A of drug company Lek had the highest turnover and closed 0.43 percent lower at 25,270 tolars on volume of 320 shares.
Overall 11 shares fell, six rose, two were unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover slumped to 39.2 million tolars from 56.4 million on Friday.
Bank UBK was the leading decliner, down 8.17 percent to 5,510 tolars on volume of 405 shares but traders said the fall was exaggerated by poor liquidity in the stock.

Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, up 9.09 percent to 14,400 on volume of 15 shares but traders said the surge was also on the back of poor liquidity and was not supported by fundamentals.
